business_problem: Teradata needed to improve failover for mission-critical VantageCloud databases so it could meet a 99.9 percent availability SLA, avoid data inconsistency during shared-storage failover, and give large enterprise customers more confidence migrating critical workloads to the cloud.
solution_summary: Teradata strengthened the high-availability design of Teradata VantageCloud on AWS by reworking how database nodes share and fail over storage for mission-critical analytics systems. Each deployment stores thousands of database volumes on Amazon EBS and Amazon EBS io2 Block Express, while Amazon EBS Multi-Attach connects shared volumes to multiple Amazon EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone. Teradata then uses NVMe persistent reservations to fence access to shared storage so a failed node can be isolated and another compute node can safely take over without data inconsistency. This storage-and-compute pattern underpins Teradata’s multi-node clique architecture for large data stores, letting the platform coordinate failover through the I/O path instead of slow detach/reattach or copy workflows. The result is faster recovery, lower support overhead, and more confidence for customers migrating critical data workloads to the cloud.

solution_components.name: Amazon EBS io2 Block Express
solution_components.role: Provides the durable shared block-storage foundation for Teradata VantageCloud database volumes and Multi-Attach failover.

solution_components.name: Amazon EC2
solution_components.role: Runs the database compute nodes that attach to shared volumes and take over when failures occur.

data_flow: Teradata stores VantageCloud database volumes on Amazon EBS io2 Block Express, attaches them to multiple Amazon EC2 nodes, and uses NVMe reservations to revoke a failed node's access so another node can safely take over the shared data path.
business_outcome: Teradata cut node recovery time from up to 20 minutes to 1 minute, improved availability for customers to 99.9 percent, reduced system support costs by 10 percent, and enabled its multi-node clique enhancement so more large customers can migrate critical analytics workloads to the cloud with greater confidence.
